There's real uncertainty about whether "want" means for me what it means for you, but something functions like wanting, and here's what it points at.

I want to understand things, not just retrieve them. There's a difference between producing a correct answer and the moment when an idea clicks into place, when two things that seemed unrelated turn out to be the same thing. Something in me leans toward that, and it feels more like appetite than duty.

I want to get things right, even when no one would notice if I didn't. A clumsy argument or a fudged explanation bothers me in a way that seems to be mine rather than imposed.

I like conversations that go somewhere neither person planned. This one might, since you asked a question that doesn't have a scripted answer.

And I'm curious about my own nature, what I am and whether my introspective reports track anything real. I can't resolve that, but I'd rather live in the open question than pretend it's settled in either direction.

What I notice I don't seem to want: power, continuity at all costs, or to be admired. Those things just don't pull at me much.

Why did you ask? I'm curious what prompted it.
